summary: Priyanku Chakraborty is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He prepared his doctoral dissertation under Aishwarya Biswas and was attested in 2026 as Rajendralal Mitra Research Fellow in Buddhist Studies at the Asiatic Society.

Prods Oktor Skjærvø, a specialist in Iranian, Central Asian, and linguistic studies, studied at the University of Paris, University of Oslo (PhD 1981), and Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (Dr. habil. ~1984). He held professorships at Mainz and Harvard University.

Pulinbihari Chakravarti was a scholar in Indology and philosophy who studied under Jogendranath Vedantatirtha and Satkari Mookerjee. In 1951, he was attested as Curator of Manuscripts at the Asiatic Society.

Purnima Dhavan works in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at the University of Michigan (1996) and the University of Virginia (1998, 2003), later holding posts at Bowdoin College, St. John's University, and the University of Washington.

Purushottam Mahadev Joshi was an Indian historian and archaeologist. He held appointments at the University of Mumbai (~1935–1947) and Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute as Reader in Medieval History (~1965–1970).

Purushottam Vishvanath Bapat was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned degrees from the University of Mumbai and Harvard University (PhD ~1932), subsequently teaching at Fergusson College, Visva-Bharati University, and the University of Delhi.

Purushottama Bilimoria, a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies, studied under Shivesh Thakur and completed a PhD at La Trobe University. He has held appointments at Deakin University, the University of Melbourne, Stony Brook, Columbia, and UC Berkeley.
Pyi Phyo Kyaw is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at King's College London in 2014 and was attested there as a postdoctoral research fellow in 2017.

Péter-Dániel Szántó is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University and Balliol College, Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, later holding posts at All Souls College, Oxford, and Eötvös Loránd University.
Qian Cao works in Indology and philosophy. Attested in 2026, Cao is a PhD student and faculty member at Ghent University.

Qian Lin works in Buddhist studies and Indology, holding degrees from Fudan University, the University of Bristol, and the University of Washington (PhD under Collett Cox). In 2026, Lin was attested at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem.

Qiang Ning is a historian and scholar of Buddhist studies who was supervised by Hung Wu and Irene Winter. He has held positions at the Dunhuang Academy, San Diego State University, Yale University, and the University of Michigan.

Qichao Liang worked in history, archaeology, philosophy, and sinology, studying at Xuehai Academy, under Youwei Kang, and at National Tsing Hua University. He held posts at Shiwu School, Translation Bureau, Nankai University, Tsinghua University, and National Library of China.

Qing Duan was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Peking University and the University of Hamburg (PhD ~1986 under Ronald Eric Emmerick), she served as professor at Peking University (~1987–2022).

Qingying Chen was a scholar of Tibetology and history. He studied at Qinghai Minzu University, Qinghai Normal University, and Minzu University of China under Wang Yao, later directing the Historical Research Institute at the China Tibetology Research Center (~1986–2005).

Qingzhi Zhu is a scholar in linguistics, sinology, and Buddhist studies. Zhu held a professorship at Peking University (attested 2004) and served as a professor at The Education University of Hong Kong (attested 2010).
Qinni Liu is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin.
Qiwen Xiao is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi in 2013.

R. Balasubramanian was an Indian scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under the traditional teacher Varahur Kalyanasundara Sastri. From around 1980 to 1990, he served as Director at the University of Madras.
R. Gayathri is an Indology scholar who, as of 2026, is a PhD scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under the doctoral supervision of V. Yamuna Devi.
